label: rem:mn-classical-parity-blind
title: Classical Murnaghan–Nakayama characters are parity-blind: proton ≡ neutron at $q = 1$
html:
Remark. Classical Murnaghan–Nakayama characters are parity-blind: proton ≡ neutron at q = 1

Remark (Murnaghan–Nakayama parity blindness). The classical Murnaghan–Nakayama recursion computes S_n characters. When applied to the S_{3A} atomic braid projection, it cannot distinguish a proton from a neutron. Both possess identical permutation cycle types.

Positive and negative crossings project to the identical S_n transposition. The q-deformed Hecke algebra distinguishes them through eigenvalue signs. The classical limit q \to 1 crushes this distinction.

The classical computation fails to predict mass splitting but succeeds as a structural diagnostic. It identifies the exact sparse partition support of the atomic braid. The full calculation uses the q-character evaluated strictly on this pre-computed support.
